source: Baker (1991) Tidal Power, IEE; Aggidis & Feather (2012) Ocean Engineering 40:10-17; Tidal Lagoon Power / Swansea Bay (2015) Scoping Report; Xia, Falconer & Lin (2010) Renewable Energy 35:1455-1468

unit.name: Generic Tidal Lagoon (Swansea-Bay-class, bidirectional bulb turbines)

A_lagoon.note: Lagoon impounded plan area (Swansea Bay ~11.5 km2). Treated as level-independent (vertical walls).

tidal_amplitude.note: Sea tide amplitude a (half of peak-to-trough range); sea level z_sea = a*sin(2*pi*t/T). Swansea Bay mean spring half-range ~4.5 m.
tidal_amplitude.source: Tidal Lagoon Power (2015) Swansea Bay Scoping Report

T_tide.note: Semidiurnal M2 tidal period = 12.42 h = 44712 s

N_turbines.note: Number of low-head bulb turbines (Swansea Bay design = 16)

D_runner.note: Bulb turbine runner diameter (Swansea Bay 7.35 m, 20 MW units)

Cd_turbine.note: Discharge coefficient for turbine flow Q=Cd*A_t*sqrt(2 g H). Calibrated to give ~rated flow at design head.
Cd_turbine.source: Xia, Falconer & Lin (2010) hydrodynamic lagoon model

Cd_sluice.note: Discharge coefficient for open sluice gates Q=Cd*A_s*sqrt(2 g H)

A_sluice.note: Total open sluice-gate cross-sectional area (used during sluicing/filling phase)

eta_turbine.note: Hydraulic+generator efficiency of bulb turbine at design head; P=eta*rho*g*Q*H

H_min_gen.note: Minimum head for generation (below this turbines idle to avoid sub-optimal low-head losses)

H_start_hold.note: Target head to build before opening turbines (holding strategy). Higher = more head, fewer hours.

P_rated_unit.note: Rated power per bulb turbine unit (Swansea Bay = 20 MW)

g.source: CODATA / WGS-84 standard gravity 9.80665, rounded to 9.81

n_cycles.note: Number of tidal cycles to simulate
